## Decisions

- ⏳ **open** `a-style-axis` `high confidence` (Matt): The design file has a Style axis with four values — User image, Gradient image, Initials, Guest — and the implementation has no such property. _Evidence: Avatar.base.d.ts declares src, alt, size, outline, disabled and decorative. There is no style property, and avatar.js renders one <img>._
  - The draft chose: Left it out of props and recorded it here
  - If wrong: Ask the Spectrum team whether the generated gradient, the initials and the guest glyph are meant to ship. Today an avatar renders whatever src points at and nothing else, so a consumer wanting initials has to draw them.
- ✅ decided `a-rebuilt-from-code` `high confidence` (Matt): The first contract for this component was scaffolded from the design file and described a row of six boxes. → The real component is a sized circle and an image, twenty-four CSS rules in total. The scaffolder had transcribed the design file's node tree — the gradient artwork, the initials text, the guest glyph and the stroke — as anatomy, laid them out as flex siblings, and hid none of them, so the preview drew six boxes side by side. _Evidence: dist/components/avatar/avatar.js is 2,193 bytes; the scaffolded contract was roughly 900 lines with 327 refusals._
  - The draft chose: Rebuilt from the implementation, as badge, button and icon were
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `a-size-naming` `high confidence` (Matt): The design labels each size with its pixel box; the code uses the rung alone. → size is "500" in code and "500 (40x40)" in the file. The value map in the size prop is the translation. _Evidence: AVATAR_VALID_SIZES is a numeric tuple; the Figma Size axis carries the labels._
  - The draft chose: The contract carries the code value and maps to the design label
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `a-sample-art` `high confidence` (Matt): An avatar with no src is an empty circle, so the preview had nothing to show. → The sample is the design file's art, not something invented. It is a slot default, so it describes what the design puts there; it is never a value the component ships with. _Evidence: exported from the Size=1400 User image variant's Photo layer._
  - The draft chose: Export the design's own placeholder photo into the package and name it on the slot
  - If wrong: The schema has no key for a media slot's sample art, so it is recorded under default.props, whose description covers the design's overrides on the instance. A `sample` key would read better.
- ✅ decided `a-image-source` `high confidence` (Matt): The renderer had no way to emit an image whose src is a prop, so the preview drew a placeholder comment. → The asset form already emitted <img src=…>, but required a manifest and field because it was built for lookup tables like the product icons. An avatar has no key to resolve: src is the source. Those two fields are now optional. _Evidence: The slot is kept alongside: it records what the design fills the picture with, including the exported sample._
  - The draft chose: Declared the image part as an asset whose prop is the source
  - If wrong: none
- ✅ decided `a-outline-attr` `high confidence` (Matt): Toggling outline changed nothing in the preview. → The image's outline rule is written against [data-outline="true"], and the prop declared no attr, so the generated component never set one. A prop that conditions styling has to name the attribute that carries it. _Evidence: The rendered root carried data-size and data-disabled but no data-outline, so the rule could not match._
  - The draft chose: Declare the attribute the styling keys on
  - If wrong: none

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.1.1`, `1.4.3`, `1.4.11`

- An image, not a control. It renders <img> and takes no focus.
- alt describes the person or entity; alt="" or decorative marks it decorative and hides it from assistive technology.
- Disabled dims the image; it conveys no state to assistive technology because the avatar is not interactive.
